It adds a few more experimental system checks (marked with 🧪) to this page that might help you find issues with your Matomo instance. There might still be a few false positives and false negatives, so don't take the results as a truth, but check yourself if something is wrong. DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckInternedStrings: It seems like you have set opcache.interned_strings_buffer below 8MB which might be a bit low. Please increase the value to 8 (Megabyte) or more depending on how many PHP files you serve and how much memory your server has available.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckJIT: As you are using PHP 8 or newer, you might want to look into enabling the JIT compiler. It might be able to speed up Matomo by a bit. It would also be great if you could report back any experiences after enabling PHP JIT.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckMaxFiles: It seems like you have set opcache.max_accelerated_files to or below %s which might be too low to keep all Matomo files in the cache, especially if you are also hosting other PHP applications. Please set the option to 7963, 16229 or 32531 depending on the number of PHP files your webserver uses.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckMemory: It seems like you have set opcache.memory_consumption below 128MB which might be too low to keep all Matomo files in the cache, especially if you are also hosting other PHP applications. Please increase the value to 128 or 256 (Megabyte) depending on how many PHP files you serve and how much memory your server has available.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckNoStatus: OPcache seems to be enabled, but its status can't be read (maybe because of opcache.restrict_api).

DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckOpcacheDisabled: It seems like OPcache is disabled in your PHP setup. OPcache stores bytecode of PHP scripts in memory and is therefore able to speed up PHP by quite a bit as it avoids loading and parsing PHP files on every request. Check the opcache.enable php.ini setting for more information.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckOpcacheEnabled: It seems like OPcache is enabled. %1$sMB of %2$sMB are used for PHP scripts (%3$s%% wasted) and %4$sMB of %5$sMB are used for interned strings. %6$s%% of requests hit the OPcache.
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckSaveComments: It seems like you have disabled the opcache.save_comments setting. This removes comments from the OPcache making it smaller, but breaks Matomo. Please set opcache.save_comments to 1
DiagnosticsExtended.OpcacheCheckValidateTimestamps: It seems like you have disabled opcache.validate_timestamps which means that PHP will never check if the actual files on disk have changed, but continue to use the cached ones. In theory, this should be no issue as Matomo invalidates the OPcache on updates and installs, but you might still want to look into this if you encounter weird issues.
